newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas futures end mixed, fronts lose.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas futures end mixed, fronts lose.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Tuesday in a typically-quiet, post-expiration session, with front months losing ground but holding above support amid little conviction about market direction.
March slipped 6.9 cents to close at $2.546 per million British thermal units. April settled five cents lower at $2.257. Others ended mixed, with some late 1997s up slightly.
"People realize March is the month when gas from storage has to come out, but the market seems pretty well-supported here by the forecasts. I don't see prices cratering," said one East Coast trader.
He said forecasts calling for mostly below-normal Northeast weather through next week should help support physical prices when February flows begin this weekend.

Traders said utilities may have opted to head into February short gas, gambling on mild weather to temper needs. They noted gas inventories in the East, still 19 percent over year-ago, appear comfortable.
"Most of the LDCs don't seem to be big buyers of February gas. They plan to pull out of storage, but if it stays cold, people may change their mind about March," a trader said.
Withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's weekly American Gas Association storage report ranged from 120 to 200 bcf.
Technical traders pegged March support along the trendline in the $2.50 area and then at the recent $2.46 low. Resistance was seen at $2.70 and then at $2.80.

In the cash, January Gulf Coast gas firmed five to 10 cents Tuesday to about the $3 level, with Feb on the same pipes talked in the low-to-mid $2.90s. Jan Midcon gained a similar amount to about $3 on colder weather in the region, with Feb quoted in the $2.80 area. New York city gate gas for Januray or February was pegged in the $3.60s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 6.9 cents to $2.238. NYMEX said an estimated 23,421 Hub contracts traded, down sharply from Monday's revised tally of 65,764.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Tuesday. February Alberta and Permian natgas expire Wednesday.

On the KCBT, February expired 1.4 cents higher at $2.621, while deferreds finished down by one to four cents. The March East/West spread narrowed by 2.9 cents to 23.6 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 731 contracts traded, up from Monday's total of 702.
